provider_query: The first YouTube video, Me at the zoo
answer:
**“Me at the zoo”** is the first video uploaded to YouTube.

1. **Upload and creator** — YouTube co-founder Jawed Karim uploaded it on April 23, 2005 (around 8:27 p.m. UTC). It remains on his channel: [youtube.com/watch?v=jNQXAC9IVRw](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jNQXAC9IVRw). [[1]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jNQXAC9IVRw) [[1]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jNQXAC9IVRw)

2. **Length and content** — A roughly 19-second clip of Karim standing in front of elephants. He says: “All right, so here we are in front of the elephants. The cool thing about these guys is that they have really, really, really long trunks, and that’s cool. And that’s pretty much all there is to say.” [[1]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jNQXAC9IVRw) [[2]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jNQXAC9IVRw`)

3. **Location** — Filmed at the San Diego Zoo. The zoo has publicly noted that the first YouTube video was shot there. [[3]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MYw_nV9vM-0) [[4]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Nq40445sn2M&pp=0gcJCR4ZAYcqIYzv)

4. **Camera** — Recorded by Yakov Lapitsky, per the video’s description text. [[1]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jNQXAC9IVRw) [[1]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jNQXAC9IVRw)

5. **Scale** — Recent listings show on the order of 440+ million views and about 20 million likes on the original upload. [[1]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jNQXAC9IVRw) [[1]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jNQXAC9IVRw)

6. **Context** — YouTube was started by Karim, Chad Hurley, and Steve Chen. Public uploads began in April 2005; the domain had been registered earlier that year. [[3]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MYw_nV9vM-0) [[5]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=SKcXEYqsX1M)

7. **Was it truly first?** — Karim has said this was the first video: he uploaded it to a test database that was then made the live database, so claims of an earlier public upload are not supported by his account. [[6]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OEzvINOXcqU)

8. **Later use** — Karim has occasionally changed the video description to comment on platform policy (for example, the 2013 Google+ comment requirement). [[1]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jNQXAC9IVRw)
